This text reviews recent progress in the operator-algebraic approach to conformal quantum field theory. It discusses how methods from operator algebras provide a rigorous mathematical framework for studying conformal field theories, with particular attention to structural and classification problems.

A central emphasis is placed on the role of representation theory in classification theory. Representation-theoretic techniques have become essential for understanding the internal structure of conformal quantum field theories, analyzing their sectors, and distinguishing or classifying models within the operator-algebraic setting.

The material presented is based on a series of joint collaborations with R. Longo. These collaborations have contributed to the development of the operator-algebraic perspective on conformal quantum field theory and to the application of representation-theoretic methods in the classification of such theories.
outputs.L4:
This text reviews recent progress in the operator algebraic approach to conformal quantum field theory, with particular emphasis on the role of representation theory in the classification of conformal nets. In this framework, conformal quantum field theories are studied through nets of von Neumann algebras associated with intervals on the circle, and structural properties of these nets provide powerful tools for understanding their representations, extensions, and symmetries.

A central theme is that representation theory offers a systematic way to organize and classify models. By studying sectors, modular tensor categories, index theory, and related invariants, one can distinguish different conformal field theories and identify when apparently different constructions lead to the same underlying mathematical object. These methods have become especially important in the classification of rational conformal field theories, where the representation category is expected to carry rich algebraic and categorical structure.

The text also highlights results obtained in joint work with R. Longo. These results demonstrate how operator algebraic techniques can be combined with deep ideas from subfactor theory and tensor category theory to produce new classification results. In particular, they clarify the structure of extensions of conformal nets and provide tools for analyzing models arising from loop groups, cosets, orbifolds, and related constructions.

The significance of this work lies in its contribution to a broader classification program for conformal quantum field theory. By connecting representation-theoretic data with operator algebraic structures, it becomes possible to formulate precise classification problems and to solve them in important cases. The results discussed therefore represent an important step toward a more complete mathematical understanding of conformal quantum field theories and their possible symmetries, extensions, and representation categories.

counterfactuals.output:
**Operator Algebras and Conformal Quantum Field Theory**

We discuss the operator algebraic approach to conformal quantum field theory, in which a chiral conformal field theory is described by a net of von Neumann algebras on the circle satisfying locality, covariance, positivity of energy, and natural structural assumptions. This framework provides a model-independent setting for studying superselection sectors, modular theory, subfactors, and representation categories, and it reveals deep connections between conformal symmetry, index theory, and tensor categories.

Special emphasis will be placed on structural results for conformal nets, including the role of modular methods and the analysis of inclusions of local algebras. The approach also offers powerful tools for classification problems and for the construction of new models, linking conformal quantum field theory with subfactor theory and low-dimensional topology.

The talk is based on a series of joint works with R. Longo.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

Recent developments clarify how locality, covariance, modular theory, and superselection sectors encode the analytic and categorical features of conformal field theories. In particular, the study of completely rational nets has connected operator-algebraic methods with modular tensor categories, subfactor theory, and classification programs. These advances provide a mathematically robust framework for understanding chiral conformal field theories, their extensions, defects, and boundary conditions, while also strengthening links with vertex operator algebras and low-dimensional topology.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
